origin.description: Linear approximation to the statistic on each bootstrap replicate.
origin.usage:
linear.approx(boot.out, L = NULL, index = 1, type = NULL,
              t0 = NULL, t = NULL, ...)

arguments.name: boot.out
arguments.text: A nonparametric bootstrap object. Frequencies are rebuilt by boot.array from its seed.

arguments.name: L
arguments.text: Empirical influence values. If omitted, they are calculated by empinf.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based position of the component of interest. If several positions are given and either t0 or t is missing, only the first is used, with a warning.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Influence type passed to empinf when L is omitted. See empinf.

arguments.name: t0
arguments.text: Observed value of the statistic. When omitted, boot.out$t0[index] is used. When t0 is supplied but both t and L are omitted, the installed function warns and then uses t0[index]; it does not replace t0 by boot.out$t0[index].

arguments.name: t
arguments.text: Bootstrap replicates used to calculate L when t0 is supplied and L is omitted. Ignored when t0 is omitted.
Further arguments passed to empinf, and from there to the statistic, when L is calculated.

origin.details: A replicate with frequency vector f is approximated by t0 + sum(L * f / n_s), where n_s is the size of the stratum containing each observation. The frequencies come from boot.array. The manual's city and bigcity examples plot the approximation against the bootstrap replicates.
origin.value: A numeric vector of length boot.out$R, one approximation per replicate.
origin.example:
set.seed(1)
x <- c(2.2, 1.1, 4.4, 3.0, 5.5, 0.2, 6.1, 7.3)
mean.w <- function(d, w) sum(d * w) / sum(w)
b <- boot(x, mean.w, R = 30, stype = "w")
lin <- linear.approx(b)
print(lin)
plot(seq_along(lin), lin, type = "l",
     xlab = "replicate", ylab = "tL*", main = "Linear approximation")

translation.description: Linear approximation to the statistic on each bootstrap replicate.
translation.usage: linear_approx(boot_out, L=None, index=1, type=None, t0=None, t=None, **kwargs)

arguments.name: boot_out
arguments.text: An object with data, statistic, stype, sim, R, seed, t0, and optionally strata and t. sim "ordinary" or "permutation" is rebuilt from seed. This does not call boot().

arguments.name: L
arguments.text: Empirical influence values. If omitted, they are calculated by empinf.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based position of the component of interest. If several positions are given and either t0 or t is missing, only the first is used, with a warning.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Influence type passed to empinf when L is omitted.

arguments.name: t0
arguments.text: Observed value of the statistic. When omitted, boot_out.t0[index] is used. When t0 is supplied but both t and L are omitted, t0 is reduced with index after a warning.

arguments.name: t
arguments.text: Bootstrap replicates used to calculate L when t0 is supplied and L is omitted.

arguments.name: **kwargs
arguments.text: Further arguments passed to empinf when L is calculated.

translation.details: A replicate with frequency row f is approximated by t0 + sum(L * f / n_s), where n_s is the stratum size. Frequencies are rebuilt from seed with the same ordinary and permutation sampling as boot.array, including column-major placement of the index draws. The generator state is restored afterwards. The example plots the approximation against the replicate number with Matplotlib.
translation.value: A one-dimensional NumPy array of length R, one approximation per replicate.
translation.example:
from types import SimpleNamespace

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from boot.influence import linear_approx

x = np.array([2.2, 1.1, 4.4, 3.0, 5.5, 0.2, 6.1, 7.3])

def mean_w(d, w):
    d = np.asarray(d, dtype=float)
    w = np.asarray(w, dtype=float)
    return np.sum(d * w) / np.sum(w)

boot_out = SimpleNamespace(
    data=x,
    statistic=mean_w,
    stype="w",
    sim="ordinary",
    strata=None,
    R=30,
    seed=1,
    t0=np.array([mean_w(x, np.full(x.size, 1.0 / x.size))]),
)
lin = linear_approx(boot_out)
print(lin)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(np.arange(1, lin.size + 1), lin)
ax.set_xlabel("replicate")
ax.set_ylabel("tL*")
ax.set_title("Linear approximation")
